observations.statement: HITL-014 is accepted as an optional, explicitly enabled UX feature with all toggles off by default; it cannot be required for correctness, verification, or progression gates, and autonomous runs are required to proceed deterministically without human approval.

Tier and phase labels are derived grouping or view concepts rather than execution authority; approval and recovery bind to a blocked runtime episode identified by run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, and an optional attempt_id.

package_complete_gate and seam_complete_gate are the canonical gate types: package gates follow completion or skip of all nodes and run package verification, while seam gates validate cross-package contracts when seam transitions are needed.
Phase, task, and subtask HITL toggles are independent and default off; their labels cannot redefine approval scope, blocked identity, recovery semantics, persistence ownership, or gate ownership.

The execution-affecting HITL configuration is one GuiConfig block persisted in redb at config:gui.hitl, with phase, task, and subtask fields copied unchanged into the run snapshot at run start and no duplicate backend-only key family.

At package or seam decision points, enabled groupings pause through the canonical blocked episode, display completion state and approval controls, emit approval and gate outcome events on approval, and otherwise remain display or configuration context rather than a competing tier execution model.

Approve and Approve & Continue dispatch cmd.runtime.approve; Decline dispatches cmd.runtime.decline and retains the same blocked identity; Skip node and Abort run map to skip_node and abort_run; abort preserves blocked and node-execution lineage.
The units provide plan migration and plan index validation surfaces and explicitly prohibit creation of WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.
Plans/human-in-the-loop.md is declared the HITL owner while referenced documents retain their own SSOT boundaries.
Context after the core identifies Dashboard warning or Call to Action surfaces and chat Assistant or direct Dashboard controls as HITL addressability consumers; this is recorded as context only.

candidate_findings.title: Grouping toggles lack an exact gate mapping and collision rule
candidate_findings.statement: The core declares independent phase, task, and subtask toggles and says each requests approval at the corresponding package/seam gate, but it never maps a grouping to a gate or defines ordering, deduplication, or prompt behavior when multiple enabled grouping boundaries coincide.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement different pause frequencies and approval ordering for the same configuration, producing incompatible runtime and GUI behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Gate trigger and failure-state contract is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: The package gate has a stated completed-or-skipped predicate, but the seam gate uses the undefined condition when seam transitions are needed; the core also does not state result schemas or state transitions for failed, cancelled, or retried package verification or cross-package contract validation.
candidate_findings.impact: Gate activation and failure recovery can diverge across executors, allowing progression to pause, fail, or continue inconsistently.

candidate_findings.title: Decision-point scope is ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-014 and HITL-017 frame approvals around package or seam decision points, while HITL-019 also refers to a blocked episode reaching its decision point; the core does not establish whether a non-gate blocked episode independently invokes HITL.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent blocked runtime states may or may not surface human approval depending on builder interpretation.

candidate_findings.title: Approval and gate-event protocol is not exact
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-019 requires canonical approval and gate outcome events on approval but supplies no event identifiers, payload schemas, ordering relative to command handling and persistence, delivery or replay rules, idempotency rule, or event outcome for decline, skip, abort, or command failure.
candidate_findings.impact: Consumers can observe duplicate, missing, or differently ordered state and may resume or render a run inconsistently.

candidate_findings.title: Recovery action contract is only partially mapped
candidate_findings.statement: Recovery actions derive from ordered allowed_action_ids, but the core gives exact IDs only for skip_node and abort_run; Retry from safe point, Start fresh attempt, Resume after prerequisite, and Replan lack exact allowed_action_id or command mappings, transition outcomes, and invalid or stale-choice rejection behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI ordering, dispatch, authorization, and recovery-state transitions can differ for the same allowed action list.

candidate_findings.title: Optional attempt identity lacks applicability and comparison rules
candidate_findings.statement: The blocked episode identity includes an optional attempt_id, but the core does not state when it must be present, how absence is normalized, or whether approval and recovery commands must match it.
candidate_findings.impact: A command can be associated with the wrong retry attempt or be rejected differently by conforming implementations.

candidate_findings.title: Configuration schema and persistence failure semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: The canonical location, field names, false defaults, and run-start copy are stated, but explicit field type and validation rules, missing or unknown-key handling, schema version and migration behavior, redb read or write failure fallback, transaction or concurrent-update behavior, and treatment of post-start edits for an active run are not.
candidate_findings.impact: Persisted defaults and run snapshots can differ after corruption, upgrade, storage failure, or concurrent GUI edits.

candidate_findings.title: GUI feedback and accessibility behavior are not specified
candidate_findings.statement: The core names completion state, approval controls, and action labels but does not define required displayed fields, enabled or disabled rules, pending and error feedback, keyboard operation, focus movement or restoration, accessible names, or state announcements.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can expose inconsistent or inaccessible approval experiences and give users insufficient feedback during command processing.

candidate_findings.title: Cross-unit dependencies and implementation consumers are not encoded
candidate_findings.statement: Semantically downstream units declare empty depends_on and unblocks arrays, and the configuration unit lists only the owner plan document as an implementation surface even though its canonical text names GuiConfig, redb, and run snapshot construction and its ContractRef names other owner documents.
candidate_findings.impact: Build ordering, integration ownership, and readiness checks are left to builder discovery instead of being machine-addressable in the PlanUnit graph.

candidate_findings.title: Accepted PlanUnits retain acknowledged multi-concern coupling
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-019 and HITL-020 are accepted while split_recommended is true, and both state that their source span contains multiple separable HITL concerns; no subunit boundaries or independently scoped acceptance oracles are provided.
candidate_findings.impact: Pause behavior, event emission, GUI controls, action dispatch, and lineage can be implemented or validated as an indivisible bundle, weakening ownership and defect isolation.

candidate_findings.title: Behavioral acceptance evidence is absent from the window
candidate_findings.statement: The stated acceptance and validation surfaces preserve source traceability and invoke plan migration or plan index validation, but the core supplies no executable runtime scenario or observable oracle for default-off autonomy, gate triggering and failure, config snapshotting, blocked-episode transitions, event emission, or action handling.
candidate_findings.impact: A unit can remain accepted under the stated plan checks without evidence that the runtime and GUI satisfy its consequential behavior.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Default-off behavior and the rule that HITL cannot gate correctness, verification, or autonomous progression are explicit.
Approval authority does not bind to tier_id, and grouping labels are explicitly barred from redefining approval scope or blocked and recovery semantics.
The package gate trigger explicitly requires all nodes to be completed or skipped, and its validation purpose is package verification.
The durable configuration owner, key, field family, default values, run-start snapshot copy, and prohibition on a duplicate backend-only key family are explicit.
Approve and Decline command families and the skip_node and abort_run action IDs are explicitly mapped.
Decline explicitly preserves run_id, node_id, and blocked_sequence while paused, and abort explicitly preserves blocked-episode and node-execution lineage.
Reject, Skip, and Cancel Run are explicitly compatibility copy only and cannot create graph-local command semantics.
The planning boundary explicitly prevents creation of WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, and production build tasks, and the compile hint disables WorkNode creation.
Document-level HITL ownership and the retention of referenced documents' SSOT boundaries are explicit.

unknowns.statement: It is unknown within this window whether the preserved ContractRefs define the missing gate, blocked-episode, configuration, event, action, or consumer details.
The exact mapping from phase, task, and subtask groupings to package and seam gates, including coincident-boundary handling, is unknown.
The conditions that make attempt_id present or absent and its role in command matching are unknown.
The exact event schema, persistence owner, delivery guarantees, ordering, replay, and idempotency behavior for approval and gate outcomes are unknown.
Fallback behavior for missing, malformed, version-skewed, unreadable, unwritable, or concurrently edited HITL configuration is unknown.
Whether the named validation commands exercise any runtime behavior is not established by the core.
Dashboard and Assistant addressability is stated only in context after the core, so exact core-owned consumer behavior cannot be established from this assignment.
